I’m a second-year B.Des UI/UX Design student who enjoys understanding people, questioning everyday experiences, and turning ideas into meaningful designs.

My design journey is driven by curiosity. I like observing how people use products, identifying what isn’t working, and finding opportunities to make those experiences better.

Beyond UI/UX, I enjoy illustration, photography, typography, branding, and experimenting with 3D. These interests help me approach design from different perspectives and bring a creative touch to my work.

I’m currently looking for opportunities to learn, collaborate, and contribute to real-world design projects.

  • Illustration
  • Photography
  • Typography
  • Branding
  • 3D

My design approach

Design is more than making things look good. It’s about understanding the problem, listening to people, and creating solutions that make sense.

I’m especially interested in turning complex experiences into simple, accessible, and visually engaging interfaces.

  1. Research

    Listen to people and study how they use things today.

  2. Define

    Name the real problem and who it affects.

  3. Ideate

    Explore many directions before choosing one.

  4. Design

    Shape flows, layouts, and visual language.

  5. Prototype

    Make ideas clickable so they can be tried.

  6. Test

    Watch people use it and note where they get stuck.

  7. Refine

    Fix what didn’t work, then test again.

UI/UX case study

Gaana

Exploring a more personal and engaging music experience for young listeners.

Project
Music app redesign
Platform
Mobile app
Research
Focus group study

Overview

A redesign concept for Gaana, one of India’s music streaming apps, aimed at young listeners.

The project looks at how a familiar music app could feel simpler to use and more personal, so listeners spend less time searching and more time finding music they enjoy. The case study covers the problem, the proposed solution, and my role and responsibilities on the project.

What I focused on

A simpler interface

Reducing clutter so the most-used parts of the app are easier to reach.

Better music discovery

Helping listeners find new songs and artists without digging through menus.

Mood-based recommendations

Exploring suggestions shaped around how the listener feels, not just what they played last.

Research with real listeners

Using a focus group study to understand what young listeners want from a music app.

Amazon Echo Show 5

HCI evaluation

Amazon Echo Show 5

Usability challenges and rule violations in a popular smart display.

Project
Personal project
Method
Heuristic evaluation
Product
Amazon Echo Show 5, powered by Alexa

Project overview

This project examines the Amazon Echo Show through the lens of key Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) principles.

The device combines voice interaction powered by Amazon Alexa with a touchscreen, creating a multi-modal experience. People can use voice commands, touch gestures, and visual feedback, which affects usability, accessibility, and how efficiently they get things done.

Why this product

The Echo Show 5 is one of the most popular smart home devices. People use it every day to set alarms, play music, check the weather, and control smart home appliances.

It combines voice interaction through Alexa with a touchscreen, which makes it an excellent example of a multimodal interface. That combination allows a thorough look at usability, accessibility, feedback, and user satisfaction. The device also operates within the wider Amazon ecosystem.

The device

Unlike regular Echo speakers, the Echo Show includes a touchscreen display, so it supports both voice and visual interaction. Its main purposes are to:

  • Provide voice and touch interaction
  • Display visual information such as the weather, recipes, and videos
  • Enable video calls and smart home control

Usability issues found

Mapping everyday interactions against HCI principles surfaced six key problems.

Effectiveness

Misunderstood commands

It sometimes misunderstands accents or unclear speech.

Privacy and security

Always listening

Always-on microphones can raise privacy concerns.

Accessibility

Speech impairment issues

Users with speech impairments may run into recognition problems.

Visibility and feedback

Listening uncertainty

Some states are unclear, so users can’t always tell if it’s listening.

Efficiency

Repeated commands

Having to repeat a command, like “Set an alarm”, wastes time.

Error handling

Unhelpful responses

Replies like “Sorry, I didn’t understand that” give little guidance.

Heuristic evaluation

Each principle was assessed for strengths and weaknesses, followed by an overall evaluation.

Effectiveness

Strengths

  • Can play music, set alarms, display weather, show videos, and control smart devices.
  • The screen confirms results clearly.

Weaknesses

  • Sometimes misunderstands accents or unclear speech.
  • May show irrelevant results.

High effectiveness, but performance drops in noisy environments.

Efficiency

Strengths

  • Voice commands are fast.
  • The touchscreen provides shortcuts.

Weaknesses

  • Repeating commands wastes time.
  • Ads and suggestions can slow interaction.

High efficiency for routine tasks.

Learnability

Strengths

  • Natural language interaction.
  • Simple, intuitive interface.

Weaknesses

  • Advanced features and routines take exploring.

Very easy to learn.

Memorability

Strengths

  • Common commands are straightforward.
  • Touch icons help recognition.

Weaknesses

  • Custom skills and routines are easy to forget.

Good memorability.

Error handling

Strengths

  • Gives spoken and visual error feedback.

Weaknesses

  • Responses like “Sorry, I didn’t understand that” give limited guidance.

Moderate error recovery.

Feedback and visibility

Strengths

  • A blue light shows when it’s listening.
  • The screen shows current activity and responses.

Weaknesses

  • Some states may still be unclear.

Excellent visibility and feedback.

Accessibility

Strengths

  • Helpful for users with visual or mobility limitations.
  • Supports both voice and touch.

Weaknesses

  • Users with speech impairments may face recognition issues.

Highly accessible.

Privacy and security

Strengths

  • Users can review and delete recordings.

Weaknesses

  • Always-on microphones may raise concerns.

Moderate trust level.

Consistency

Strengths

  • Core Alexa commands work consistently.

Weaknesses

  • Third-party skills may behave differently.

Mostly consistent.

User satisfaction

Strengths

  • Convenient and engaging.
  • The screen enhances the experience.

Weaknesses

  • Privacy concerns and occasional ads can reduce satisfaction.

Generally high satisfaction.

Brand identity and web

Tropicana Reimagined

Freshness in every sip. A rebrand that makes a classic juice brand feel fun, youthful, and modern.

Project
Rebranding project
Tagline
Sip your sunshine
Deliverables
Logo, packaging, landing page, merchandise, stationery

About the project

Tropicana is an American brand famous for its juices. Its logo has changed many times since the brand began in the 1940s. I created a new identity for the brand while keeping the visual recall customers already have of its logo.

Concept

The original logo looked traditional, so I redesigned Tropicana to feel more fun, youthful, and modern.

The new identity is fresh and playful, built to appeal to Gen Z and young consumers.

The new logo

Purple stands out

Purple makes the brand feel modern and distinct on the shelf.

Rounded, friendly letters

Rounded letters give the brand a friendly, fun personality.

An orange for the “O”

The orange-shaped “O” signals fruit and freshness, and the juice splash adds energy and movement.

A flowing blob

The blob shape feels organic, like flowing juice.

Packaging

Landing page

Each flavour gets its own hero: orange, grapes, apple, and mango, all with the line “Pure goodness in every sip!” The page highlights 100% juice, no added sugar, and no artificial flavour.

3D product design

Stylus Reimagined

Unique, precise, intuitive. A stylus sculpted for creativity.

Project
Product concept
Tool
Autodesk Fusion 360
Focus
Ergonomics and form

Overview

A unique stylus designed in Fusion 360 that blends ergonomics, aesthetics, and precision for a natural, creative experience.

The design combines ergonomic comfort with a sleek, sculptural form. It focuses on smooth curves, balanced proportions, and a tapered tip to create a tool that is as functional as it is distinctive.

Design principles

Ergonomic grip

Shaped to sit comfortably in the hand during long sessions.

Precise control

A tapered tip for accurate, confident strokes.

Distinctive design

A sculptural form that stands apart from ordinary styluses.

Balanced proportions

Smooth curves and even weight so it feels natural to hold.
